doc.title: Quincy Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Mentors and the brass and band instruments he tried at thirteen
summary: Asked about mentors, Jones lists Basie, Ray Charles, Clark Terry and Nadia Boulanger, plus Stravinsky, Bernstein and Copland, and recalls trying drums, sousaphone, horns and trombone before trumpet in his early teens.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: When you think that you’re really one of a kind – who were the mentors? Who were the people? Because I can’t even find a model for what you do.
It’s a combination of a lot of things, from Basie to Ray Charles to Clark Terry to Nadia Boulanger. They don’t get any better than her.
I was going to ask about that.
Add Stravinsky and Bernstein in there, and Copland and – what is it? – all the guys.

I just wonder, how do you shift gears? Like, for instance, not only do you transcend the time thing, but you deal with all kinds of styles. I’m wondering, who are the mentors? Did you study the scores of somebody like Ellington or somebody such as . . .
Of course. But that was all part of the thing from the very beginning. That’s 13 years old. It was the first time I got in my arm – when I started playing trumpet – first I

started drums – percussion and everything – sousaphone, tuba, b-flat baritone, e-flat alto. I played french horn and Silent Night. I remember that when I was about 13 or 14. And played trombone, because I was no dummy, and I knew in the marching band, the trombone players were up there next to the majorettes.
